text:
mira (eng-platform): heads up — got a support ticket where the customer's console shows ~2.1M tokens for the day but billing shows ~3.4M. customer is heavy on streaming + tool calls. suspect retries or truncation accounting edge-case.

sam (billing): can you paste request IDs / logs? usually retries show up as separate attempts in billing unless we dedupe.

mira (eng-platform): pasted minimal logs from their session:

```
RequestID=rc-9f2  attempt=1  stream_chunk=1/3 tokens_out=120
RequestID=rc-9f2  attempt=2  stream_chunk=1/3 tokens_out=120  # client retried after recv timeout
RequestID=rc-9f2  attempt=2  stream_chunk=2/3 tokens_out=250
ToolCallID=tc-44   parent=rc-9f2  tokens_tool=30
RequestID=rc-9f2  attempt=3  stream_chunk=3/3 tokens_out=90  # server resumed
```

mira (eng-platform): customer saw 120+250+90+30 in console = 490 tokens, but billing shows 840 (double of the first chunk).

jordan (eng-runtime): aha — when the client reconnects and we resend the first chunk, we currently attribute tokens per successful output stream write. Retries can produce duplicate outputs that get counted if the previous attempt had already been persisted to billing. We don't currently have a dedupe key for streaming chunks.

olivia (eng-platform): that aligns with a second issue: tool calls triggered inside streaming callbacks can be retried by the client without an idempotency token, so we might bill the tool invocation multiple times.

sam (billing): proposal: require an idempotency header for tool_call and stream session start (X-Redwood-Idempotency). if missing, bill normally. if present, dedupe within a window.

arjun (console): UX question — if we dedupe at billing layer, console needs to show both raw attempts and deduped billed tokens so customers understand what happened. we should add a per-request "dedupe_reason" flag to the console timeline.

mira (eng-platform): suggested headers/snippet:

```
POST /v1/chat/stream
X-Redwood-Idempotency: rc-9f2
X-Redwood-Streaming-Chunk: 1/3
X-Redwood-Stream-Session: s-7b2
```

jordan (eng-runtime): implementation notes: we can use (session_id + chunk_idx + idempotency) and keep a short TTL cache (idempotency_window_ms, default 5000ms) to dedupe duplicate token writes. need to decide: dedupe only identical outputs or any re-send of the same chunk index?

sam (billing): prefer deterministic dedupe: if response bytes are byte-for-byte identical and request idempotency header matches, mark subsequent attempts as deduped. fallback: if body slightly different, treat as separate. we can't risk under-billing.

olivia (eng-platform): where does truncation fit? customer also said we truncated final output server-side due to token cap and they re-requested with truncated prefix which produced additional tokens. do we bill for truncated tokens that were generated but not delivered?

jordan (eng-runtime): current flow: we bill by tokens generated by the model, regardless of whether they were later truncated or dropped by the router. so yes, generated-but-truncated tokens are billed. we log a "truncation=true" flag but console doesn't surface it well.

mira (eng-platform): customers get upset when they see apparent double billing from retries; transparency helps. my proposed rollout: 1) require optional idempotency header; 2) introduce server-side dedupe window for streaming/tool_call backed by exact-content match; 3) add console columns: raw_tokens, deduped_tokens, billed_tokens and a per-request note for truncation/retries.

arjun (console): UI mockups look fine — show a small yellow "deduped" chip next to events, expand to show attempts list. can we add a filter in the usage page to include/exclude deduped tokens?

sam (billing): one more constraint: reserved/dedicated customers expect strict accounting so any dedupe must be opt-in per-tenant until we validate. we should gate dedupe behind tenant flag.

jordan (eng-runtime): ops constraints: cache RAM cost is small if we store 64-bit hash per chunk per session with TTL. worst-case churn on high throughput customers needs testing. I'll prototype in canary.

mira (eng-platform): quick RFC items to agree on:
- header names and semantics (idempotency vs session id)
- dedupe TTL default (5s?) and per-tenant override
- exact-match vs fuzzy-match policy (exact only initially)
- console visualization + filter
- controlled rollout start with hosted customers + opt-in for dedicated/private

sam (billing): +1 on exact-only, 5s default, tenant opt-in. add billing audit logs for any dedupe decisions.

olivia (eng-platform): I'll draft the RFC and include example logs and console mockups. can someone from runtime volunteer to prototype the cache and hash logic? @jordan?

jordan (eng-runtime): happy to. will post a short PR with a prototype cache and a small perf microbenchmark.

ops-bot: Scheduled canary rollout job created for rc-dedupe-proto (env: canary) — ETA 2026-02-18 03:00 UTC.

mira (eng-platform): thanks all — next steps: olivia write RFC, jordan proto, sam add audit hooks, arjun prep console filter. I'll tag the ticket and link here when ready. :thumbsup:
